page.layout: One page of text in a single column; marginal references in the left margin beside lines 6 and 9; a faint printed note at the left margin lower down, not legible.

main_text.p: sed stillam & guttam significat. Si quid igitur ex nomine esset eruendum sanctius longè diceretur, ut stillæ maris, maris amplitudo & vires absurdissimè tribuerentur ; sic virgini Mariæ, Dei creaturæ, creatoris Dei gloria: Cui omnes gentes quasi ‏מ‏ mar, stilla situlæ & quasi momentum stateræ deputatæ sunt. Itaque merito ait Deus, Gloriam meam alteri non Dabo. Ac propterea quis non videat, Coftere,quàm toto aberrescælo, quando eum scriptionis tuæ præfigis scopum, ut lectores potentes sint exhortari in doctrina sana & eos qui contradicunt arguere? Nam si hæc doctrinæ vestræ est sanitas, quæ ægritudo? Si lumen vestrum tenebrę sunt, ipsæ tenebræ quantæ? Oftende sodes hujus erroris vestri vel apicem in sacris literis, & aspersam idololatriæ notam abfterferis, pijfque rationem poscentibus, satisfeceris abundè. Sed illud tum demum eventurum est, quando luci & tenebris convenient. Quod ut, ex orthodoxæ antiquitatis monumentis, clarius patefiat, insigne Epiphanij, aduersus hanc Mariolatriam & sanctorum invocationem,

page.notes: Marginal references read "Ezech. 40.15." and "Esa. 48.11." as far as legible. The Hebrew word in the line "Cui omnes gentes quasi" is not reliably read and is given only approximately. The final word "nem," at the foot is a catchword-like fragment; it is part of the last line. Faint margin print at lower left is illegible.
